Trail: Mizzy Lake Trail – Algonquin Provincial Park
Time: 6 hours (from parking lot to finish)
Conditions: Cool, overcast, minimal bugs very very muddy.

We completed the full Mizzy Lake Trail in exactly 6 hours. The cool, overcast weather made for comfortable hiking with almost no mosquitoes — definitely a plus. However, the trail was extremely muddy in many areas, and several sections were slow and slippery, especially between markers 8 and 11, which was particularly challenging.

The trail is also very rugged, with constant rocks, roots, and uneven footing, so proper footwear and good balance are a must. BRINGS WALKING POLES ! We noticed a long gap between markers 10 and 12 — Marker 11 was missing or we just missed it as you must go off trails to avoid the mud traps. While we never felt lost, it was long enough to make us double-check that we were still on track.

Wildlife sightings included loons along the boardwalks and, most memorably, a moose crossing Highway 60 as we finished — definitely the highlight of the day.

Overall Thoughts: Beautiful in spots, but extremely muddy and tougher than expected. We’re glad to have checked it off the list.

We have been hiking Algonquin for 10 years and have completed every trail in the park (many of them multiple times) but we had never completed Mizzy Lake. So we decided to change that today. It was a beautiful warm, sunny day. We started out at 9:30am and completed the trail just before 1:30pm. Total hike time was 3h 57min which included stops to take pictures and to have a quick lunch break on the trail. Although the trail distance is stated as 10.8km, it was actually 12km as per my Apple Watch. We did not complete the extra 2km trail to the bear dens. The trail starts out rugged with lots of rocks and roots. It then progresses to a nice easy hike on the old railway with spectacular views of various lakes along the way and the potential to spot various wildlife. The trail ends with another rugged hike through the forest but with lovely boardwalks and views along the water just before the final forest push to the parking lot. Elevations are minimal on this trail. The trail is muddy throughout. Beware, at the 3.5km mark there is a short section of the trail under water. The water was above the ankle line so we had to take our shoes and socks off and walk through it for a few minutes. It was well worth it as after this section was the lovely flat old railway section with tons of lookout points for wildlife. We saw a raven in a tree and moose tracks in the mud but no moose or bear were seen by us today. We both used our walking sticks which we were particularly thankful for on this trail as it made the journey much easier. Wearing proper hiking shoes or boots is a must. As it was a Saturday, the trail was well populated with people which probably contributed to the minimal wildlife observed. Additionally, dogs are not allowed on this trail to increase the likelihood of viewing the abundance of wildlife. Overall this is long, rugged and muddy trail but with beautiful views of various lakes and bodies of water that it made it all worthwhile. Please note, if your predominate interest in hiking Algonquin is to view the fall colours, this trail would not be a top choice. Booth’s Rock, Centennial Ridges, Track and Tower and The Lookout would be our recommendation for that. We are happy to say that we conquered Mizzy Lake and would definitely recommend it to those who are fit, have good balance, and don’t mind getting a little bit muddy.

It rained 2 days ago so it was really muddy/soggy. Lots of hills, roots, rocks - might be challenging for someone with knee/ankle concerns.  Very nice trail with many opportunities to see wildlife. It got pretty buggy around noon.
Some mud and bugs, but nothing extreme. Beautiful hike.

One of my favourite hikes in the park! With proper hiking boots you’ll have no issues passing some of the soggy sections. Passed on going down the “Bears Nest” side trail and the hiked ended up being closer to 12km.
12.2 K not 10.8 K. No bugs.  Still muddy. a great day hike for us.
Some mosquitoes beautiful trial

Beautiful trail- trail guide (stored under the main trail map at the start of the path is a highlight!) Reading about the different flora, mammals, and birds provides context for all the various terrain seen. We saw several birds, including a blue Herron. 
Went in the middle of the day and probably for that reason didn’t see moose/small mammals. 
Tips- there was minimal rain in the days before we went and it was still really muddy/boggy. The worst of it is the first 1.5 miles and basically the whole last 3 miles- so waterproof hiking boots helpful. 
Do not let the 1.5 middle section along the railroad path and boardwalk lull you into thinking that the last 1/2 will go faster!
Rocky
Muddy. Lots of logs that you have to balance on to keep going

Started at 0900 and came out at 1335. Lots of mud and one bridge partially underwater but its still doable. Probably not a good idea to do this trail without some bug repellent and waterproof footwear. The bugs weren’t that bad for us but we wore cream and used a portable repellent after reading previous reviews. Saw few animals.

Bright sunny day but many sections were wet and required you to cross over by treading carefully over rocks or logs. There were even one of two boardwalks below the water line in very short sections. We didn’t get wet, but if you are at all unsure of your footing, pick another trail.
Great trail still, but even more challenging at the moment.

This trail is a former railbed. Flat grade finished with gravel makes the hike an easy one. Traverses through birch forest and open ponds/lakes. We started this hike at 19:00 hours and spotted a young moose eating water Lillie’s at the marked waypoint!
Lots of bugs and roots

Went at 8am. Trail was extremely buggy - make sure to lather up the bug spray. Even with bug spray though, most won’t find the hike enjoyable due to the number of flies. I sped through the trail and finished in 2hr45 just so I could escape. At one point after the railway bed, there is a large downed tree completely blocking the trail, so be aware of that. It rained a ton last night so many parts of the trail are flooded as well.

Beautiful trail. It was hard for my out of shape self but the youth we were with found it moderate. 

Buggy at spots and sunny at others. Worth it. We didn't see any animals but we also went on a super hot day.
I finished in 2hrs 37 minutes. I was swarmed by flies from post 3 to 8. Highly recommend all forms of bug protection. I did see a moose!
Muddy in a few places, and quite buggy. Bug hats are a good idea. Still a great hike though.
Formidable
Really buggy this time of the year. But a lot of lady’s slippers

Two beginner hikers completed this route in 3.5 hours. Bring boots with good ankle support, as the trail is full of roots, rocks, and muddy patches. The scenic spots weren't exactly what they were made out to be. The hikes were not worth the views. The whole trail had a ridiculous amount of mosquitos.

Beautiful, long trail. Clocked around 14 km on all trails, as opposed to what the park signage says of 10.8 km. Spotted turtles and birds and was lucky enough to see moose on the roadside while driving to the trailhead.  The trail has a lot of muddy areas; boots are highly recommended.
We completed this trail with 2 11 year Olds in 4 hrs.  Decent trail, a bit muddy in certain spots. The bear den is a waste of time... didn't see anything there.
This trail is great with a nice easy walking part on a rail trail in the middle. Lots of turtles and often see Moses here too.
Lovely scenery but maybe wait until it dries up a bit. On May 1 it was more rock hopping and tree climbing over then it was hiking. Tons of evidence of moose though!
Muddy and still quite a bit of snow on the path once you get into the dense bush. Couple places washed out but still easily crossable.
Nice trail still lots of snow and ice very wet and slippery

Some of the trail crossings are underwater, and other parts turned into marsh. Completed the trip longer than usual because of the thawing conditions. 

The trail itself is great but I’d wait another couple weeks for the snow melts completely, and the water levels return back to normal.
Winter hike was super cool. Be prepared to sink in the snow on the lake. It piles high from the wind on the lake, and is soft. I loved it but some say that makes me crazy.

Great day to be on the trail. Cleats highly recommended for the main trail as it is getting icy with the warming weather.  The Bears Nest Loop is very deep snow and not a lot of traffic,  so you will need snowshoes.
Snowshoes recommended for certain sections, particularly in areas where there is blowing snow (near lakes).

Amazing Saturday hike! Weather started crispy cold in the morning and got a bit warmer, with sun shining through the trees at times. 
Hike can be done without snow shoes, but get ready to bury your entire legs in the snow sometimes! 
No wildlife spotted

We started the trail at 10:30 two days after a major snowfall.  The track in the snow was there in the woods, but was blown over in open section.  It took us 6 hours, including stops to look at wildelife and for lunch, getting back st 4:30, very tired and with sore knees. in my case.
We saw an ermine in its white winter coat, an otter, woodpeckers and lots of moose signs at Dizzy Lake.

Hiked the full loop today with ice cleats, though snowshoes would be helpful in a few places. The snow is fairly well packed, but there are instances where it's a little deeper. A few muddy patches and several areas where the trail is washed out, or trees are down on the trail however still passable. Saw an otter and a few Canada jays on the rail trail. Hiked several times and never tire of this place - the alltrails guide on elevation change is totally wrong though, it's nowhere near 600m, maybe 100-200 tops.

Only walked in about 1/3 of the way and then back out. Beautiful trail with lots of variety. Will definitely go back to do the full trail.  Saw mama moose and calf right right on the trail as we rounded a bend! Made our trip!

More then 10.8 and 12km east side is a walk in the park west side is wet, rugged and for people who want the adventure. Very wet trail that crosses puddles and streams. In winter, snow may not be well packed. Hiking poles or a walking stick recommended.

One of my favourite trails. I've completed the full loop a couple of times - relatively challenging (long!) but lovely. This time I only went in approx 1km, sat by one of the first lakes for a bit, then doubled back to the parking lot. Quick in/out is nice if you're only up for a short hike.

Great trail, well maintained and well marked.  Enough benches and places to stop to eat and take a break.   A couple of suggestions for Algonquin Park though.  We did the "blue" trail, it's almost 14 km, park info ranges from describing it as 10 km, 12 km, and 13 km on the map in the trail guide, might be handy to let people know the actual distance.  The trail was marked really well, no chance at all somebody could get lost as long as they followed the markers.  the last 2 or 3 km were poorly marked, we had to stop several times to find a marker.  Aside from that, it was a great almost 5 hours, no moose but saw a fox, and had a really good day on the trail.  Recommended for all!
Gorgeous trail with many landscape changes! Snowshoed it last winter during family day long weekend and think back on it fondly and frequently! Helped to have poles and snacks, took about 4 hours.

Although this trail is long it was very easy. About 40% of it is an old rail bed so it's very flat and wide. You'll breeze through it. Even though the old rail bed allows for easy walking this does not mean you should go fast. The trail goes through a few lakes and wetlands so there will be lots of opportunities to see wildlife. Once you're back onto traditional Algonquin forest trail. You'll be rewarded with classic views from the lake side sections and crossing of marshes. It's an easy to moderate hike. Easy because of the old rail trail and moderate because of the length.
Great…

It's a okay Trail unfortunately with the Arowhon Pines Resort at the top end of the trail this has provided road access.  In the past the road was exclusive to registered guests only but that is no longer the case.   The best chance of seeing wildlife would've be to drive up there early in the morning and park in the area just before the resort.  I haven't done this Trail for nearly 20 years and it's grown in particular the rail section but unlikely to hike it again.
Beautiful trail lots of lakes. Did not see any wildlife though
Nice mix of flat and inclines. Long stretches on flat terrain with potential for full sun exposure in the afternoon so make sure you’re prepared for the sun.
Great trail, but be careful on some of the boardwalks, there’s some broken boards.

Soooooo long … i’m an amateur hiker and it was relatively easy, a bit rocky and tree rooty at times, quite scenic, was hoping to see moose/bears but all we saw was a few partridges and chipmunks. maybe go earlier in the morning to see moose. :).
trail was good. got rained on but prior to that wasn’t buggy or muddy. the extra 2km optional loop is definitely not worth it as it doesn’t feature any water or lookout, just trees.

Posted sign says 10k but it is longer.  If you go counter clockwise from the parking lot the trail starts fairly smoothly and ends with last third being very rooty, rocky and up and down.   The overall trail is broken up nicely with pine packed trail, roots and rocks and some boardwalks.
Pretty great trail for beginner hikers that want to go on a scenic hike!
Hiked the trail today, from about 10-4 pm. Sunny, breezy, really nice experience. This trail ended up having lots of beautiful spots, especially for those who like seeing turtles and water life.

Beautiful trail, we did it backwards which was cool. Wasn’t a fan of the flat marsh area as it was a haven for flies and sun on this 35 degree day, it was Death Valley. Other than that section the bugs weren’t bad at all and it was a beautiful trail to hike. We did it in about 3 hours with stopping twice, once because we had to wait for a female moose and her calf to move as they were blocking the trail. Definitely recommend.

It was my second time doing this trail. Great forest trail, bogs and you get to pass by 7 lakes. Relatively easy, but long, with lots of tree roots. Wear proper footwear and bugspray! 
Awesome morning hike!!
Very flat. Flattest in the park.

Great trail. Lots of variety, just quite a lot longer than the guide lets on. I clocked just over 12kms to finish (in just under 4 hours). Bugs weren’t an issue with bug spray. The mud you’ll hear about wasn’t an issue either - everything was fairly dry. I did see many spots that would be muddy if we had rain, so be ready
Wonderful trail. We saw a moose!

Great outing overall! I'd rate this as the second toughest of the Hwy 60 trails, after Centennial Ridges. It's long and the second half can be a bit technically challenging - not too bad for ups and downs compared to other trails but so many roots and rocks. Lots of bugs today, too, especially along the rail bed. Bug spray is a must, as are good shoes.

On the plus side, zero mud despite a heavy downpour yesterday. Every other time I've done part or all of this trail I've dealt with intense mud throughout along with light flooding here and there. And it's a gorgeous trail.

(Note on length. My recording is wonky.  As others have noted, the trail is about 12km. I started out at 10 and got back to my car shortly after 3, including breaks for water, snacks and taking pictures.)

The trail had beautiful views and was a very nice hike. Pretty buggy in places, especially when following the old railway, but not much worse than you’d expect. 

Overall views were great and we did get to see some wildlife tracks and turtles. Keep an eye out near Dizzy Lake to find some pitcher plants! There weren’t many climbs and the trail was well maintained. We tracked it at 12 km so make sure to leave plenty of time to finish before dark.

Spent 90% of this trip in frustration, very much inside my own head due to the flies. So much so, a really pretty lady running the trail absolutely scared the shit out of me as I didn't hear her approaching .Nothing says confidence, calmness, coolness or manliness like screaming and recoiling in terror like a 8 year old girl on sight. 1 star for being the site of such an embarrassing experience
Flies are crazy
Trail was absolutely beautiful. I tracked it as 12.2km instead of 11.7. Deer flies are really bad around Wolf Pond section.

Beautiful trail, lots of lakes and wildlife to see. Took me about 3 hrs and 45 mins to complete, bring lots of water and good hiking shoes as there are lots of roots and quite a bit of incline on the second half of the trail.

We like doing this trail. Lots of scenery and chances to see wildlife. Only some turtles and birds for us this hike. Lots of moose prints. 
We were happy to have on our bug spray and good hiking shoes.
was great  beautiful  look  out  points and  moose  prints  almost  everywhere  very clean   not  many people
Great scenery, but you can’t stop too long because bugs will be all over you…

Lots of beautiful sights. Follow lakes and creeks and meadows. Lots of forest too. Bear Nest side loop is interesting. Some mud, with one section where the boardwalk was broken and you had to get wet. A section of bad bugs. Not much wildlife today, but a beautiful walk!

lots of bugs and mud. make sure you bring a hiking stick and bug spray. sections 7 to 10 was quite the slog for novice hikers like us, lots of roots and smalls rocks to navigate aroundThe views were amazing, lots of animal tracks

Not a bad hike, but definitely more on the muddy / buggy side. Took us just over 3.5hrs, but likely because minimal stopping due to mosquitoes feasting on you if you stop moving. 
Lots of Moose foot prints but unfortunately no sightings.

My crew and I chose this trail as it stated it was a great place to view wildlife... Algonquin spirits did not disappoint. Lucky enough to have two amazing moose sightings and plenty of photo ops. This trail took us approximately 7.5 hours to complete by the time we stopped along the way for all of the gorgeous scenery. Mizzy trail takes you along several lakes and bog areas as well as through the dense woods and over some boardwalks. It was a nice mixture of broad scenery with beautiful forest. Mainly flat with few inclines. Trails were well marked for the most part and only had a few areas with rocks and roots to navigate. Definitely wear appropriate footwear as it is quite muddy especially after rain.
Optional side trail to apparently see some bear dens which we did not try. Lots of animals tracks and scat along the way...clearly a well used area for the animals. Plenty of openings to sit and have lunch along the trail. Be sure to bring food and water as it is a challenging trail and marked difficult due to length and diverse footing. Was absolutely worth it. I was skeptical at first as I prefer a hike with cliffs and outlooks but Mizzy Lake was not a disappointment! Suggest that you go early in the AM to see wildlife. We set out around 7am and finished around 2 or so. It was a fantastic trail. Would absolutely do it again.

Nice long trail, trail is actually 12km took me 4 hrs to complete
Some muddy areas, but was able to navigate around.

A challenging but rewarding trail. I didn't have the time or energy to complete the entire route this time around, instead did an out and back of approx 4-5 km altogether (ignore the reading here - the app kept cutting out).

It's generally well marked and only a couple of overgrown sections. The terrain can be tricky and there is a lot of mud, but not a ton of elevation. I've found that waterproof hikers and poles for extra stability are a huge help when navigating the extra mucky bits. Oh, and bring bug spray! 

It's not the easiest but truly is a fantastic trail. Spectacular views across all the lakes and marshes. Definitely worth the effort.
It was great a little longer than I thought
Very muddy at some points. Recommend hiking boots.

The trail was nice and quiet, with a little sprinkle of bugs. lots of areas still wet but a non issue for us seasoned hikers. loved all the water, the turtles...saw lots of moose droppings along the 12km trail
Took about 5 hours with good breaks

Amazing! Lots of turtles bathing in the sun. Beautiful views of small lakes and ponds. Took me over 4 hrs… with breaks. There are lots of benches to sit on. It’s a long hike and muddy so be prepared. It’s 12km.

Although longer in duration, this is not a moderately difficult trail, it’s quite easy. A lot of low lying areas with water to navigate, so good pair of hiking boots is￼￼ a must. All in all, a really pleasant trail. Allow for approximately 2.5 hours to complete.￼

It was amazing! With different scenic points to look at, lots of different wildlife, different walking terrain and diffferent footing from really rocky to flat. But holy moly is there a lot of mud and icy patches right now.
Great hike lots of great views, some wild life, and nice boardwalks. Be sure to wear hiking boots
ice almost gone. great seasonal conditions. some mud, but everything passable.
Very icy and slippery in spots still
beautiful but some icy spots...takes longer than normal
Challenging trail in the spring. Small patches of ice, but lots of them. Certainly made parts of the trail very difficult and slippery. Lots of animal droppings, but mo major sightings today!
mix of snow and moist trail only small patches ice

LONG trail in the winter. The old rail portion is brutal with a bunch of slushy snow on the ground and the path veers off in a portion without reception which is frustrating. If you go counterclockwise visit the first 2-3 lakes, they are beautiful. If you plan to in the winter be prepared to take longer than 6 hours to finish
An absolute delight of a forest! So quiet and still. Perfect almost spring weather. Trail is easy to follow, a few icy spots, as one might expect this time of year.
Challenging - second time snowshoeing

I did the trail this morning and it took 4 hours with lots of photo and breath stops. I did the trail counterclockwise and it was easy going until about half way along the old rail line. The other half of the trail was not nearly as packed and was pretty hard slogging. No wildlife seen except for rabbit, weasel, wolf and moose tracks. Some moose poop too. Stick to the centre of the trail. The snow on either side is really deep particularly along the boardwalks. Glad to have my power bank to recharge my phone and power my camera heater. -23 today. Crampons are a really good idea

Very pretty, but definitely not maintained in winter as advertised. The parking lot was unplowed, a large tree blocked the entire start of the path, and we had to turn around due to the trail becoming unmanageable. Still, gorgeous views.
Good kept trail! A few icy spots, but you can walk around with caution. Fairly easy, took about 4hrs and was 12.2km in length. Did not see any wildlife, but plenty of fresh tracks around!

Awesome winter hike. Trail was in great shape. No need for traction aids. Relatively flat and not technical at all. There is a long boring stretch on an old rail line, but besides that, a great way to train for your summer adventures.
Lots of tree’s down over the trail, unfortunately didn’t see any wild life. Has some great views though.
A little more challenging than we thought and had to turn off at Weldwood Rd.

20+ trees down along the trail but other hikers has already stomped down a path around. 11.1KM logged on this at 4.5h (includes a 30 min lunch). Barely any animals out but may have been a noisy family in front of us and time of day. Not too hilly, not too technical. Not slippery. Decent snow cover to cover any ice. Traction was ok. Great trail and will do this one again for sure. Arrived at noon with sunset at 4:39PM. Cut it close but well prepared.
trail was amazing! lots of habitat types and wildlife sightings if you go early! great for winter birds
It is actually a 12.2 km hike. Beautiful coniferous trees covered with snow
Trail was very snowed over and lots of trees fallen over the main route. Stunning scenery with sightings of wolves. Very enjoyable!
Flooded over in a lot of spots

Unlike some of the other Highway 60 trails, Mizzy Lake Trail's beauty is subtle.  No significant lookouts or waterfalls, but a greater sense of remoteness.  It is a test of ankles and calf muscles. Even though no significant elevation change,  there's nary a step that is flat; always with roots or rocks underfoot (apart from the stretch along the old railway).  Mud wasn't too bad on my hike but there many areas requiring careful stepping over some wet spots. The friendly (and noisy) raven at Wolf Howl Pond and ubiquitous Canada Jays were a highlight until I stumbled upon a pair of resting bullmoose (bullmeese?).  What a thrill.

Good trail - I was disappointed I couldn't finish it today. I only made it an hour in, then doubled back - not because of trail conditions or difficulty, I just realized after a couple of kilometres that my energy levels weren't up to a 4-5 hour hike. 

The mud was as I remembered from when I completed the full trail last year - so, so much mud! - but it's manageable with good hiking boots. I had poles this time, which were super helpful.

Aside from all the mud, there are the usual roots and rocks but not a lot of elevation. It's quiet with a mix of forest and lake/marsh side. Not overly busy.
Little muddy but very nice!

Beautiful Trail.  Not too difficult. Took us longer as we did it in the pouring rain, but great because we met very few other hikers on the entire trail.  Fall colours were stupendous.  Pictures do not do the leaves justice.  You have to see it to believe it.  Some roots, small rocks, and lots of mud,  but still manageable in the rain.  Lots of small wildlife throughout the trail and near the end we walked up onto a HUGE bull moose.  He just stood there looking at us and then slowly and nonchalantly walked away
Trail was under water

Not a single thing to complain about! The trail was basically empty and really scenic, but do be aware of the mud and water on the trail at times. I set myself the challenge of not getting my shoes dirty and while it was definitely challenging, it is possible if you really want to.
nice ...better than expected, even the west side.  no moose sighted .. denied again :-)
Nice trail. Somewhat technical. It was very muddy. At parts we were following the trail that was essentially a river. Nice views. Wear rubber boots. Nice colors
fun trail. sustained but not too hard. many benches along the way which was nice. listed as 10.8km but our tracker is showing more like 12km
Great trail…. However listed as 10.8km and more like 12.5km

Hiked it in the afternoon after a very heavy rainfall and 1/3 of the trail was submerged.  I suspect there are wet areas even when there hasn't been a heavy rainfall.  Trail was nice with some climbs and flat areas.  Had a nice close encounter with a grouse and rabbit.
amazing, the ponds were superb. saw some ravens upclose. enjoyed my company the most.
Beautiful trail. Nice mix of technical and some easy walking.  Wash rooms at the car park and lots of cool places to stop and take a break. I would rate as moderate.

Fantastic trail - good way to spend the better part of a day. The trail is specifically designed for wildlife viewing so no dogs are allowed. I was told that moose, deer, beavers, and a variety of birds could be seen from this trail but sadly missed out on all but some great birds. 

The east side of the trail makes for pretty easy hiking - I would rank this section as easy and saw many people of all ages and builds in the area. this is where a large portion of the nature viewing is regardless and if you're hoping to see Moose than the east side is your best bet. If you're looking for an easy time, just go out and back in this side. 

The west side does get a bit more challenging but I would still only call it moderate. you get similar views, a great spot to stop for lunch, and more of a traditional hike in before the trail ends.
Challenging spots but overall felt like a long walk compared to Centennial Ridges. Unfortunately no wildlife sightings despite a 8am start, but still lots of good views and a nice trail!

Took us a little over 4 hours with a lunch break. No luck with any animal sightings but got to see some interesting footprints. Terrain was swampy, challenging, and needed maintenance at times but nowhere near as challenging as Centennial Ridges. Beautiful landscapes.
Great hike. No moose today but great scenery. A bit muddy but not as bad as the past. 4 1/2 hours including a lunch break.

Great hike! Challenging due to a lot of tree roots and rocks on the path. A lot of the trees and shrubs are overgrown which make it a little more difficult to cross. We went on a day that rained a bit so it was quite muddy. Lots of lakes throughout the hike which are absolutely beautiful. Boardwalk parts throughout and at the end make for a nice relief from the tree roots. Not too many mosquitos. Went at 9am on a weekday and took 4.5 hours with a couple breaks. Didn’t see any animals whole we were there! Would recommend for a challenging longer hike!
My boyfriend and I did the trail today! Moderate trail but not many great spots for pictures!
Awesome.  Tough going

The trail is fun but also tricky because there are so many different types of terrain. You twist and turn through the forest stepping over many tree roots and rocks, i could see how it could get very muddy pretty easily in some areas.  And just a couple spots were overgrown and felt in maintained however there are many bogs that you get to relax a bit by walking on a boardwalks and sitting on countless benches to catch your breath or enjoy the peaceful water. There’s a sign saying at times you can see bear nests at one spot (no dogs allowed) but thankfully there’s none to see right now because we didn’t want to run into a bear but we hoped to see a mouse, no such luck. We saw grouse 3 times, chipmunk, frogs, toads, geese, ducks, a few other small birds. We are fast hikers and only took brief breaks for water and it took us 3.5 hours but it could easily be a 5 hour hike if you’re not on a mission. I would do this trail again and pack a snack and stay longer. We only saw 1 other person and we went in at 7am out at 10:30am. Bugs weren’t bad and we didn’t use bug spray just walked through a lot of spider webs the first half of the trail.
Another good time on this trail even with seeing no wildlife.  It was great that we finished this with no muddy hiking boots, or feet.  Great conditions, lots of bugs on return trek.
Great loop - 2/3rd are in forest with roots and rocks. Total distance is about 12.5km  and elevation around 140m not 500m
Beautiful trail with varied scenery. There’s a guide book at the trailhead for a self guided tour of the different things you’ll see. It’s was a little muddy but not bad and almost no bugs.
Great hike to see wildlife, saw lots of tracks and activity but no sightings. Be prepared for mosquitos and mud
Beautiful trail.  Quite technical at the start and end, but theres a nice break on a rail trail at the midpoint.  Not too much elevation on this one.
Incredible trail, but super muddy today because of all the rain.
Very muddy!! Also not 11km more like 14km. Had a few over grown areas and trees down blocking the trail.
Probably would have enjoyed it more if it weren’t for the mosquitoes and mud! Not many great look out points either. Overall wouldn’t do again.
Muddy but lovely
This is no moderate trail. More on the difficult side, and very muddy when I went. Beautiful lookouts. mosquitoes tried to have a feast of me. thank God for bug spray.

The first half of the trail is great. It was worth while seeing the meadows and looking for moose (didn’t see any today). The rest was walking through the forest which is nice. Bugs were not too bad and less than expected this time of year. Mainly between markers 8 and 12. We saw lots of signs of wildlife with tracks and droppings. We saw a loon, turtles, and beaver. We took 5 hours and GPS said 12.3km.

Take this trail if you are interested in experiencing wildlife. Hikers that we passed had seen a black bear, mink, and moose prints! We saw a grouse and experienced a 4.5 hour fly fiesta, along with many scourges of mosquitos along the way. By the time we made it through, we felt like blood donors despite being covered in bug repellant. Challenging trek.

A long hike but a good one! We unfortunately did not see any moose, although some more committed folks had seen one out earlier at dawn. We did see moose tracks, painted turtles, herons, a garter snake and a variety of water fowl. There are portions of the trail where the black flies are relentless so prepare accordingly! Walking the trail with several stops ot took us about 5 hours!

Good trail lots of different lakes and scenery along the way. There were signs of wildlife. Moose tracks, bear paws, possibly wolf tracks. Come prepared with good bug spray as the mosquitoes were vicious. Some areas with deer flies. Overall it took 3 of us 3 hours and 30ish minutes to complete with some stopping. The terrain is a bit hard to navigate and requires some attention to detail. Overall 8/10 would recommend.

My husband and I are fluffy people and have only been into hiking for the past year to give some background. We love nature and have only been able to hike for 2 hours before attempting this trail. It is our friends favourite and the reviews were fabulous. There were so many roots and rocks that all I did was stare at the ground to walk so I didn’t fall or twist my ankle. I wore mosquito netting as they were not great and there were relentless deer flies chasing us. There were no benches or places to stop that we saw. We got about an hour and a half in and realized we both were not enjoying ourselves and that much further would be pretty hard for us. The return was another hour and a half. We saw people who love the trail and talked about all the great spots to see so I’m sure it may have gotten lovelier. For these two fluffs was too much

This trail was amazing! There were 3 of us who went and we were going at a decent pace and it still took us around 3-3.5 hours to complete the whole trail. There were many lookout points and we saw turtles, butterflies, and a moose! We were able to get close enough for good pictures of the moose!
Saw a moose  The trail was a fun challenge, not too hard.
Beautiful as always and a lot dryer at this time of year. Remember your bug spray though as it will be needed
Beautiful and manageable trail that took 3 adults in their 30s 3 hours and 15 minutes to complete. We saw turtles, butterflies and a moose. Mosquitoes were out in full force, so come prepared.

This is a demanding trail that brings you to several breathtaking vistas. I saw a moose on my way to the trailhead and hoped to see more, but not to be. Part of the trail is an old railway bed where I ran into two different ladies who were moose spotting as well. They knew the easy way in via the Arowhon Road. Although the walking was easy on the railway bed, the mosquitoes were far more intense. They're a special Algonquin industrial breed that didn't bite (massive amounts of Deet) but attacked like deerflies.

If you are not an athlete, doing this whole trail is difficult. Aside from the old railway bed portion it’s walking up and down over tree roots and rocks making it  hard to enjoy the scenery. Proper footwear is a must! Was there a couple days ago and bugs are bad but not too bad with repellent. I took off one star because the trail is about 30 min too long and my toes started to hurt. Also I couldn’t spot any posts after half way but trail markers are good. It took us 4 hr and 30 min with breaks.
That being said it was a wonderful experience! I finally saw a bull moose in the water at the wolf howl lake (farthest part from the entrance) and he didn’t seem bothered by us at all. Saw turtles including a snapper, brown snake, toads, squirrel and many many birds! Also some pretty orchids! Serene!
A nice mix of terrain and scenery. Lots of turtles, jays, chipmunks, squirrels as well as deer and moose tracks.
Great trail. Lots of birds, turtles, grouse, and a brief glimpse of a fisher (amazing!)
Awesome trail with about 5 different lakes and ecosystems. You see something new around every corner. Took about 4.5 hours, 10/10 recommended

Beautiful and peaceful view, 9 lake/ponds along the trail with a good variety of terrains, lots of mosquitoes in May. Saw some turtles in the ponds. Although the trail is rugged in most parts and can be muddy in some areas, that’s what makes it more interesting. Feels like walking in wild forest. We really enjoyed the trail. Highly recommended!

covers lots of different types of terrain but mostly walking over tree roots and logs. muddy in many parts but you can find a way through. less maintained than other trails but makes it more fun and feels more wild. saw some turtles and moo's tracks. took us 3.5hours with a couple breaks
Better than expected- great day!
Variety of terrain. Beautiful views of surrounding lakes. Great hike. But it takes time.
Loved the pitcher plants. Wish I had’ve saw a moose. Wear water proof boots the trail is wet in a lot of places still.
Finished! It was a knee-buster! Lots of moose scat, ruffed grouse, friendly ravens, and another hiker saw a bear last week.

It was about a 4 hour hike, at a good pace, with a few stops along the way. This time of year, it was quite muddy, and a few fallen trees to get around, but absolutely worth it for the gorgeous scenery and serenity you experience along the way. It’s a mix of forest, old dirt road and boardwalks through open wetlands. There were minimal bugs at this time, saw some turtles, curious ravens, and a lot of moose poop and prints. Overall a bit of a work out but worth it.
30-40 trees fallen on the trail, throughout. very muddy. nice boardwalks and evidence of moose and wolf

Demanding but rewarding. Very muddy at times. You had to make your own path at points and there were quite a bunch of trees that had fallen down over the paths. But the sights were glorious. We did it in 8 hours going slow and enjoying ourselves but even briskly this would take 6 min. We started at 7am and I would recommend that! We saw a loon and a beaver too. Highly recommend this trail if you have the footing and stamina to conquer it

Really unkept and a few fallen trees, so be careful to stay on route to avoid not getting lost. 
Saw lots of wolf poop, bear poop, and moose poop!

We can appreciate some of the other recent comments - Mizzy can be a brute ... wet, muddy, fallen trees.  Terrific this time though (late March) - with the snow melted enough that snowshoes and crampons weren’t required but enough snow and ice left to cover over most of the wet parts.  Many gorgeous moments.  It’s a workout though ... took us five hours with a couple breaks.

Probably the most "wild" /unkempt trail I've been on in the park. You'll have to limbo at least a half dozen times. Snow is melting and slippery and your foot will go into the snow dozens of times anywhere that's not canopied. Boardwalks are frustrating as you balance on the soft snow or slide off. By the end you just want it done (it's not quite as interesting as the other long hikes, as it's mostly ponds). But, because it's so wild and rugged you do feel badass, and I did see a couple of moose not far from the trail, along with Wolf tracks. Still pretty, in other words. I did not run into anything "impassable" at the 10-11km Mark as a previous reviewer but there was one downed tree at around 11km that I had to walk around to the left. Kinda hard to spot so maybe that's why.
The snow is turning to sugar.  Very slippery.  Some of the bridges a little tricky.  Gorgeous day though!!! Feeling blessed!!

Went on Saturday (Feb 27) and found that it was a dead end at around 10KM in, had to make our way all the way back to the start.  Also saw wolf tracks near the end, so be careful if you're out there!  Other than this very recent bit of information, it was a tremendously beautiful hike.  Make sure you're equipped for the snow or have snowshoes.  Enjoy!

nice trail for a longer winter hike. seems a bit longer than the 11.1k advertised. we recorded about 13.2k. packed snow for most of the trail. we did it without snowshoes, they would have been helpful in some spots. highly recommended.

I LOVE this trail in all seasons it’s incredible!!! Always see different wildlife tracks, and I know many types of wildlife are often spotted on the trail. It really is so diverse, from climbing through the bush, to on the boardwalk over the marsh, to open areas. So much to see around every corner!

Stunning hike. If you go counter clockwise on the trail, the first half is quite easy. Lovely groomed trails. The second half was very hilly and convoluted. Total hike time was about 3:06 with lots of stops for photo ops. I would come back here in a flash.
Carley says its a nice trail.

Very beautiful. Snow everywhere! About 11 km hike with not a lot of steep surfaces. Walking in the snow makes you a bit more tired than usual so don't forget to pack some snacks. Strongly recommend doing it in winter!
Loved!!!! So beautiful. We did part of this trail after the freshly fallen snow. Was not an icy trail. Extremely picturesque. Lots of animal tracks. Will definitely be back for this one

Hiked the trail in high boots and it seemed like those before us also only used boots. There were some parts where snow shoes would have made it a bit easier, but the trail didn't seem wide enough for them. Overall a beautiful challenging trail in the wintertime just from the sheer distance trudging through snow (ended with almost 12km). Minimal elevation change. There were definitely spots that were soakers, so just keep an eye out! Make sure to start early especially if you're a slower hiker!
Great trail no grooming during winter understandably. Some markers father then others so some back tracking but to be expected.
Really wer but still a great hike!
long, lots of swampy parts, hilly and beautiful
quite challenging at times , muddy , felt like an obstacle course , the winner gets dry and clean shoes . overall great trail , tests your balance and decision making skills :)
Unseasonably warm day gave us a wonderful hiking experience!  Mud in numerous places, but trailblazers who preceded us led us in the right direction - finished in over 4 hours.
Part of trail is very muddy even though sunny and no rain for a few day. It really slow you down in the muddy aera. We finished in about 5 hour.

Trail was very muddy at times. We didnt opt for the extra side trail, and we clicked 11.8km because of having to go around the trail so much. Based on the mud/wet and slippery roots/rocks I would rate those parts difficult. however there were some very easy areas including some board walks, and a trail section that was completely flat/dry with no obstacles that  ran a fair length. Nice hike! Didnt see a whole lot of wildlife (only: squirrel's, partridge, a raven, chickadees, and a frog), but still worth it. Would love to come back next fall to see the fall color here.
great trail. challenging but not too hard. lots of muddy goodness
Enjoyable quiet hike.  It was very wet and had to detour around some parts of the trail but that is normal for this time of the year.  It took us 4hrs and 15 minutes to complete.
Excellent trail. Very clean and very muddy. Be careful in the morning. Lots of ice/slippery conditions.

The trail was amazing though we didn’t know how long it would take us we did our math wrong and figured 2 hours.. this trail took us 5 hours yesterday we managed to do this with no stoping, because we didn’t bring food, or water again we thought it wasn’t as long as it was clearly we were not thinking. Very wet and muddy, we went yesterday. Expect to get wet and with the paths being mostly water it definitely turns the trail into a hard instead of “moderate” our phones says we did 14km on this hike. We would do it again definitely with the proper things. Also though we didn’t see many animals we saw blue jays, red squirrels and a chip monk. We did however see fresh Wolff poop and a fresh very fresh set of Wolff tracks so be carful when walking.
Nice trail. Good scenery. Muddy, recommend waterproof hiking boots
Was extremely wet and tough sledding
Muddy, difficult and longer than expected

Really nice trail. First half is pretty easy but the second half definitely gets harder. Pretty muddy and wet in some spots but overall not terrible. Did this hike with my dad, nice with the fall colours
Awesome trail. Full of wildlife (moose, beaver, grouse, foxes...)
somewhat muddy, start early. worth it. this is about 13 kms

Trail was a bit muddy in spots but easily manageable. Do wear hiking shoes or boots.  Trail guide was full of interesting information - a great publication.  Trail was close to 12 km without the extra bear nest side trip. Fairly busy but never crowded.
Great Hike, be prepared for very wet areas

EXTREMELY muddy. It rained the day before, and the trail was real bad. We turned around just after 2km because of the mud. We even had proper hiking gear and found this trail too muddy to enjoy. Mizzy lake was really beautiful though.
Nice walk but no real wow something anywhere. Very, very muddy on Sept 5th. Some parts of the trail are even flooded  Feels like it’s time some parts of this trail would have a bit of love.

I knew from reviews to expect more mud than other trails but I wasn't expecting that easily half the trail, if not more, is heavy mud/pooling plus several streams to cross. A few spots seem almost impassable. (Refer to pics.) As it is, the terrain is uneven (the usual roots and rocks) so the mud just adds to the slipping anxiety. Your feet will get thoroughly soaked with mud, even in good weather. I'd avoid this in the rain!

To be honest, if I'd known what to expect, I might not have attempted it...but I'm so glad I did. It was challenging - mentally and physically - but that was part of the reward. It's also beautiful and so, so quiet (I only saw six other people). It's not an easy trail but don't let that stop you.

P.S. It's listed as 10.8k but I clocked around 12.5. Not a big deal.
P.P.S. Bring a change of shoes and socks for afterwards!

quite Hilly, can be boggy so make sure you go during a dry spell. my fit bit read 12.3 km for this hike, but we had to do a lot of weaving on the trail to avoid mud. still worth it beautiful lake views etc etc.

Wear your boots.  much of this trail is mud and water, in rocks and roots.  I'd score this trail higher if not for the condition of the trail.  otherwise it's a great hike past a few small lakes. a portion of it is an old rail/road way past some nice lakes.  the first 2 to 3 km are easily 60% mud.  with lots of mud and water throughout the rest of the trail.  yes, it's nature, so if you don't mind a slow going slog through mud and water then this is a great trail.  saw a river otter, and a man-eating black bear. (I'm pretty sure)
Longer than posted at 11.9 Km.  Very root and rock covered.  Difficult trail.  Bring your legs and a great pair of hiking footwear.
Some wet areas, but great views of various wildlife!!!

Trail ran this one in Nike frees. Lots of rocks/tree roots so good spatial awareness is key. Very muddy in some parts as well. Only some bugs/flies in the exposed sun/flat section right now. Majority of the hike is under tree cover. Nice views of various lakes. Some elevation change but nothing super intense. If you're a fit hiker, I'd consider this easy instead of moderate. I've found Algonquin's hike difficulty ratings pretty conservative. Finished in just over 2 hours. Recorded 11.8km so it's a bit longer than posted.

Great trail in all seasons. A little muddy in sections at present and a few flooded sections which are passable. Several buggy patches as well; trousers or bug spray recommended. Saw moose just off trail when doing this in winter, and beavers in the summer. 

The elevation change is far less than stated, seems to be a glitch on the return. Overall around 200m of undulating terrain.

Some nice views, but lots of mud along the trail and a few places where beavers decided they want a new pond. Elevation isn't bad, but it can be difficult to menouver the terrain. Took just under four hours to complete.

Really liked this trail.. well marked and really nice views along the way.  Liked the trail map which outlines the different areas.  Some muddy sections but it's close to water with lots of trees and was expected.  Didn't see alot of wildlife but I felt really good being able to complete this one.
great hike, muddy in areas, we spotted a moose and her baby in the distance

Loved it! We expected it to be really muddy since it just rained and stormed the day before our hike. It was a little muddy but not nearly as bad as expected. Trail is easy to follow and was fairly quiet. Good chance for spotting wildlife...we heard a bear groaning in the bushes... the forest is quite dense...take a bear bell or mase just in case. Beautiful scenery and the hike was long but not too difficult. I clocked over 12km.

Good trail. We were a little disappointed in the difficulty as the middle part of the trail is a long super easy stretch used for service/research vehicles. However, that part has neat views of the marshland. We came prepared after reading reviews and bought $14 bug shirts at Walmart. I think the bugs weren’t bad today so we didn’t use it until after the easy stretch when we didn’t feel like dealing with buzz in our ears anymore. We hadn’t been bit up to that point, but I could see how the bugs could get bad! 

It’s been dry lately so the trail was fine but I imagine regularly it’s a floor is lava in the forest sort of situation. Be prepared for mud!

Trail mostly wooded, with some boardwalks. The middle part of the trail has sandy paths and a lot of deer flies. The rest of the trail definitely has mosquitoes, but is a bit more bearable than the deer flies. Bug spray necessary. Definitely has many marshy/boggy areas and lakes, with wildlife sighting opportunities. Since we went out around 1030, we didn't see any moose or beavers but we saw a few herons! Reviews saying its muddy in some places are right (it goes through so many bogs and marshes) - we went when it had been dry the last few days, and there were still some mud areas you have to skirt around, though not impossible at all. Might not recommend the day after a rain

Good trail, would say it’s pretty moderate toll over the last half. First half has the best ponds/lakes for bird viewing. Recommend bringing binoculars! The deer flies around the lake area were intense and not very enjoyable. Bug spray is a good idea

It was really good trail. Somewhere are really hard, somewhere are really easy. There are too many wet area. You need water proof hiking shoe. There are too many mosquitoes and they are really hungry. You have to use "off" or something like that. You can see some wild animals. Views are perfect. You can walk in 5 hours. You need water, food and snacks.

This was a very demanding trail, even though it’s claimed to be moderate. The scenery is great, you’ll spot a few moose across the lakes from the designated hiking paths you take, but I just can’t get over how muddy it was. There’s mud literally everywhere, and it’s lowlands kind of mud, which is squishy and very wet. 

The mosquitoes here are also extremely aggressive considering the land around the lakes has become wetlands, so ensure you bring a lot of DEET or whatever you use.

Beautiful trail, passes by a few lakes. some sections are boardwalk, some cleared flat trail and some sections are rocky. We managed to complete the hike in 3 hours, at a fairly quick pace with stops only for water. There were a lot of bugs (expected at this time of year) so our stops were few and quick. we saw snakes, turtles and a moose. It was a perfect Sunday hike.
Saw 5 moose, a heron, and a turtle!
Wonderful trail saw lot of wildlife ( moose, turtles, snake, beaver). Aparently there was no one on the trail befr us today. Its bit challenging and do bring a bug spray.
Took about 4/5 hours with some rest time and a lunch break. Somewhat muddy, but there's good views and the guide is nicely informative.

Went on a muddy day end of May and it made some of the terrain challenging. Definitely underestimated the length, due to the amount of rocks and roots along the path it took much longer than I had anticipated.


Amazing challenge though with fantastic scenic points littered all across the trail.

Beautiful trail with lots of different vegetation. Lakes and forest, not very strenuous in terms of altitude changes but you need to watch your steps at times, lots of roots and rocks on the oftentimes narrow trail which makes it interesting. Also boardwalks through beautiful wetlands and a very easy part on an old railway. Took us 4.5 hours to complete with breaks for lunch and to look at the scenery. Bit muddy in certain places in the middle of May.
Beautiful trail, lots of signs of wildlife such as deer, moose, red squirrels, jays, beavers. No pets allowed.

Hiked 28Dec, a clear day with little recent snowfall. Never quite sure what to expect in Algonquin, but this trail is absolutely beautiful. We used ice cleats which made the whole thing a lot easier - 4h30 with plenty of stops. Id really recommend them in similar conditions, there was a lot of ice. As others have said, plenty of wildlife tracks (and squirrels) though we were fortunate to spot a male bull moose on the way back to the lot, just 30-40 metres off the path! Magical

Very tough trail in the winter. Due to the amount of elevation change in the wooded area, it takes much longer than one would think. Some great sights halfway through of the lakes but almost nothing notable on the second half which makes it tough to finish.
Great trail, tough at times especially the last quarter as you’re in the woodland with no great views. Lovely marsh lakes.

definitely a beautiful hike. didn't see any wildlife however beautiful landscapes. best advise, wear comfortable hiking shoes. as it is a long hike. it took us 5 hours. there is a lot of roots and rock sand some places are very muddy. regardless we enjoyed it.
nice scenic areas, very rocky and lots of roots. took just over 4 hours stopping for snacks

Pretty straightforward. Saw a loon and some turtles. Apparently is quite good for spotting moose, and some other people on the trail in the morning saw a wolf (!) but for me was average. Hit or miss I suppose!

Great trail for someone looking for a bit more than an easy walk in the woods. Wouldn't say its difficult but there are lots of spots with short steep climbs and downhills. Rocks and roots are the footing on the trail with short areas of boardwalk. We hiked with another couple and 6 kids ages 8-13. The only tough part of the trail was the was the old railroad where the deer flies were relentless. Once back in the bush they were fine. We hiked in running shoes after a good rain a couple days before and made out just fine.

My wife and I have been waiting 12 years to do this hike and we finally got to do it today, it did not disappoint! We took our 9 and 12 year old children and they made the trek as well. We didn’t see any major wildlife but we did see tons of tracks in the mud along with some screams/callings in the distance. I tracked the whole hike on my watch and I was close to 7.6 miles and this app and the book I had both said under 7, I’m not sure which it is but just a heads up. None the less it was a great hike and we really felt like we got to see part of the park that we really wouldn’t see any other way. July 24th 2019.

I left a comment on this hike but can’t relocate it. In summary this shorter bit of the Mizzy lake trail with naturalists Peter and Basil was extremely educational.  Talked of turtles, butterflies, moose and their signs of presence, birds (warblers, heron, and this one intelligent crow), tree frogs ‘spring peepers’, foxes, wolves, moths, and more.
You follow swumps and lakes so lots of roots and mud. I don't recommend it on a rainy day or even after a few rainy days
Beautiful trail, muddy and roots but that's also the fun of the trail. We was several turtels, squirrels and a moose. Be sure to wear good shoes.

Took us 4.5 hours at a fairly steady pace. Parts of the trail were very muddy, overall very rocky/lots of roots... make sure to wear good hiking shoes!  Saw lots of painted turtles, signs of moose and deer but unfortunately no sightings.  Lots of great views regardless!
Nice trail with plenty of wildlife.
This hike is awesome. There's a lot of snowy and icy sections along the trail so be prepared
Great place, i went there in summer and it was wonderful. I saw also a big moose near me, like 2 meters.

I wanted to love this trail. We hiked it in early November, and it may as well have been early spring. There was mud and mucky stuff all the way around, and we probably had to veer around these very wet areas at least 50 times in the course of the hike. Also there were at least six trees down across the path. If the path were way drier, and clearer, it would have been a great. Beautiful views, but not worth it when it’s this wet.
Great hike, we made it in 3 hours despite crazy rain! Btw. It is just 11km!
One of my favourite Trails... Excellent for Scenery and Wildlife in all Seasons... Medium intensity...

Great trail! Not too difficult because there is little incline. For the most part the trail is along the edge of the lakes. Beautiful lakes with many chances for viewing wildlife. We saw a few herons, ravens, spruce grouse and an otter. I suggest wearing some shoes suitable for mud! We took about 6 hours to complete, including a lot of time to stop and look for wildlife.

Another great trail. Bit steep at times but well worth the climb to the lookout. 
Don't forget to show your parking pass while hiking. The park wardens are always on the lookout.
Easy trail, and very nice. started out mid morning and it was not busy. I enjoyed the quiet peaceful hike
Nice Ontario trail.  If you hike in deep enough you’ll see moose.  We saw hearing we saw dragonflies it was a moderate hike with some challenging parts and we would definitely do it again.
little overgrown in spots, but a wonderful test of endurance.
This trail is an awesome day trail lots to see and you might even get to see a moose!
Too many mosquitoes, very aggressive even with repellent product AND lemon eucalyptus essential oil ! And so much mud too, very slippery. (September)

Great trail for wildlife viewing. Dogs are not allowed due to the abundance of wildlife. We were fortunate to see a pine martin on this trail and it was just as curious about us as we were about it. They are normally reclusive, so it was a fun and unique experience.

A very long and beautiful trail. Make sure you start early in the day and give yourself atleast 7-8 hours to experience the wildlife and the ponds.
I completed this trail in June. Almost 30% of the trail was flooded due to rain and increased water level of the ponds resulting in alot of mud and bushwhacking. 
Be prepared.

Very easy hike & was worth it even though I didn't see a moose but you do see a lot of their poop! 

For my full review subscribe to my blog 
www.wandering-dog.com

A really nice walk that traverses a variety of habitats, such as ponds, bogs, hardwood forest, spruce groves and pine barrens. I went at a very leisurely pace to look for wildlife and did it in about 6 hours; it can easily be done in half that time but then you'd miss out on what you could see.This is the longest of the park's interpretive trails so I would suggest to make a day of it and enjoy.The guide here says the elevation gain is over 2000 ft; that is far from true. The walk is mostly level with minimal ups and downs. Part of the trail is on an old railroad bed and boardwalks are placed over the wet areas. I would still wear a heavy pair of boots as other parts of the trail can get pretty wet and muddy. Be sure to take the side trail near the north end of the loop, it's about a 30 minute detour that goes to what are called "bear's nests", explained in the guide you get at the trailhead. On my walk I saw Spruce Grouse, a Red Fox, a bull Moose and literally hundreds of turtles basking in one of the ponds. Note that dogs are not allowed on this trail so as not to disturb the wildlife.

This is an 11km trail, and no dogs are permitted due to a high population of wildlife spotted regularly on this trail. There are at lest 9 ponds that are seen during the hike. The trail can be tricky if a long hike cannot be handled, but overall, if it's taken at the right pace its doable. Bear spray is suggested to be taken with you.
Bug spray was definitely needed.

Beautiful scenic landscapes! Saw a lovely beaver near its dam. Lots of evidence of moose. Trail is very muddy right now, and some of the trail markers are knocked down and harder to spot so problem-solving is needed. Definitely recommend!
